title: fix(ci): verify the restored Console dist's spec injection in release.yml and save its cache only on success (#9709)
body:
Fixes #9709

## What was wrong

`release.yml`'s `publish` job restores the vendored Console dist under the **same repo-scoped cache key** `ci.yml`'s Console Pin Gate uses, and carried neither of the two protections `ci.yml` carries around it:

1. **No `check:console-injection` step.** `scripts/assert-console-spec-injection.mjs` runs *inside* `build-console.sh`, which `if: cache-hit != 'true'` skips — so on a cache hit nothing asked whether the dist this job is about to **publish** bundles this tree's `@objectstack/spec` rather than the published tarball. `check:console-sha` answers only "which objectui SHA this dist claims", and it deliberately exits 0 when there is no dist at all.
2. **The combined `actions/cache@v6` action**, whose post-step saves **even when the job failed**. `build-console.sh` writes the SHA stamp *before* it asserts the bundle canary, so a canary failure left a stamped-but-broken dist on disk that the combined save then seeded the shared key with. This is the exact rationale `ci.yml` records for its own split restore/save.

The two compose: `ci.yml`'s console job is paths-filtered (the pin, the build script and this gate's own sources — not `packages/spec`), so "the ci.yml gate catches it first" holds only when a PR happens to touch one of those paths. A release artifact could ship with a stale or poisoned console dist and nothing red to say so.

## The change

`.github/workflows/release.yml` only — 34 insertions, 2 deletions, one file. Both halves are spelled exactly as `ci.yml` spells them, because the point is that both consumers of one cache key apply one check.

**Step order in `publish`, before → after** (indices from a YAML parse of the job's 19 steps):

| before | after |
| --- | --- |
| `Cache vendored Console dist` (combined `actions/cache@v6`, id `console-dist-cache`) | `[10] Restore vendored Console dist` (`actions/cache/restore@v6`, **same id** `console-dist-cache`) |
| `Build vendored @objectstack/console SPA` — `if: cache-hit != 'true'` | `[11]` unchanged |
| `Verify Console dist stamp matches pin` — `pnpm check:console-sha` | `[12]` unchanged |
| — | `[13] Verify the restored Console dist bundles this tree's spec` — `env: CONSOLE_DIST_CACHE_KEY`, `run: pnpm check:console-injection --require-stamp` |
| *(combined action's post-step: saves even on failure)* | `[14] Save vendored Console dist` — `actions/cache/save@v6`, `if: cache-hit != 'true'` |

The step id `console-dist-cache` is **kept**: `git grep console-dist-cache` finds exactly two references, both inside this block, and renaming it to match `ci.yml`'s `console-dist` would be churn with no consumer.

## Why the save is now unreachable on failure

Actions steps default to `success()`, so step `[14]` runs only if `[10]`–`[13]` all succeeded. Verified mechanically rather than by eye — a YAML parse of the job, walking the window from the restore to the save:

```
  [10] Restore vendored Console dist (keyed on the objectui pin) | uses=actions/cache/restore@v6 | if=- | coe=- | env=-
  [11] Build vendored @objectstack/console SPA                   | if=steps.console-dist-cache.outputs.cache-hit != 'true' | coe=- | run=bash scripts/build-console.sh
  [12] Verify Console dist stamp matches pin                     | if=- | coe=- | run=pnpm check:console-sha
  [13] Verify the restored Console dist bundles this tree's spec  | if=- | coe=- | env=CONSOLE_DIST_CACHE_KEY | run=pnpm check:console-injection --require-stamp
  [14] Save vendored Console dist                                 | uses=actions/cache/save@v6 | if=steps.console-dist-cache.outputs.cache-hit != 'true' | coe=-
RESULT: steps inside the console window carrying continue-on-error / always() / failure(): 0
RESULT: remaining combined actions/cache@ steps in publish job: 2 -> Setup pnpm cache | Setup Turbo cache
```

The save sits immediately after the console assertions, not at the end of the job — matching `ci.yml`, and deliberately. What the entry vouches for is *the console dist*, and every question this repo asks of a console dist has been answered green by step `[13]`. A later failure in the publish steps says nothing about the dist, and deferring the save to the end of a job that ends in `npm publish` would mean a run that failed to publish also failed to bank a console build it had fully verified.

The two remaining combined `actions/cache@v6` steps in the job are the pnpm-store and turbo caches — different caches, deliberately untouched, as are the `actions/cache@v6` uses in the `version-pr` job.

## The six key sites still agree byte-for-byte

`git grep -h` over both workflows, piped through `sort -u`, collapses all six occurrences to **exactly one** distinct string:

```
${{ runner.os }}-console-dist-${{ hashFiles('.objectui-sha', 'scripts/build-console.sh') }}
```

Line numbers as they stand on this branch (the card quoted `ci.yml:1439` / `ci.yml:1485` / `release.yml:491`; `main` has moved a long way under it, and there are now six sites, not three, because both files also pass the key as `CONSOLE_DIST_CACHE_KEY`):

| file:line | site |
| --- | --- |
| `ci.yml:1827` | restore `key:` |
| `ci.yml:1890` | `CONSOLE_DIST_CACHE_KEY:` env |
| `ci.yml:1903` | save `key:` |
| `release.yml:1106` | restore `key:` (this PR) |
| `release.yml:1130` | `CONSOLE_DIST_CACHE_KEY:` env (this PR) |
| `release.yml:1142` | save `key:` (this PR) |

`CONSOLE_DIST_CACHE_KEY` is not cargo-culted: `scripts/check-console-injection.mjs:818` reads it, and `remedy(cacheKey)` uses it so the refusal message names the real key an operator has to clear. Passing it is the difference between a failure that tells you what to evict and one that prints a template.

## Verification

- **YAML parse** of `release.yml` with the workspace's `yaml@2.9.0`: OK — 4 jobs, `publish` has 19 steps.
- **Step-order / reachability walk**: the block quoted above.
- **`actionlint`: NOT AVAILABLE** in this container (`command -v actionlint` → not installed). Said rather than skipped silently.
- **Control-byte scan**: `grep -naP '[\x00-\x08\x0b\x0c\x0e-\x1f\x7f]'` over the edited file — no hits.
- **The added step is not vacuous, and `--require-stamp` really reaches the checker.** `check:console-injection` is a two-command script (`... --self-test && ... `), so it is worth proving pnpm's trailing arg lands on the second invocation rather than being swallowed. Running the step's exact command in this worktree, which has no `packages/console/dist`:

```
$ pnpm check:console-injection --require-stamp
> node scripts/check-console-injection.mjs --self-test && node scripts/check-console-injection.mjs --require-stamp
✓ check-console-injection --self-test: 36 assertions over real fixture trees (real evaluate() path)
✗ No console dist at packages/console/dist — nothing to verify, but a dist was required.
EXIT=1
```

  Both halves shown: the flag is forwarded (the echoed command line carries it), and it has teeth — the same invocation without `--require-stamp` exits **0** on this tree, which is precisely the vacuity a publish lane must not accept. In `release.yml` the step sits after `pnpm run build`, so `packages/spec/dist` exists and the stamp-expiry re-check (the one assertion that reads this tree) can run rather than refusing.

## Gates

Derived, not recalled: `node scripts/pm/dispatch-gates.mjs --repo objectstack-ai/objectstack --commands` from this worktree, which reads the change set from git itself. **21 families**, all run.

RAN-PASS (21/21), each read from the gate's own verdict line, exit code captured before any pipe:

```
pnpm check:agent-test-spelling · check:declared-population-live · check:node-version
check:pm-dispatch-gates · check:pnpm-acquisition · check:pnpm-filter-targets
check:required-contexts · check:shard-attestation · check:stall-guard-budget
check:stall-guard-headroom · check:workflow-status-functions
node scripts/check-aggregator-roster.mjs · check-position-name-fold-loaders.mjs
check-required-contexts.mjs · check-self-test-wired.mjs · check-self-test-workflow-commands.mjs
check-shard-attestation.mjs · check-step-collectors.mjs · check-whole-set-label-write.mjs
scripts/docs-audit/check-drift-comment.mjs · scripts/pm/ci-failure.mjs --self-test
```

Four of them read the edited file directly and say so:

```
✓ check-step-collectors: 390 `run:` steps across 30 workflow(s); 3 step(s) run 2+ independent self-tests, all of them through a collector.
check-workflow-status-functions: OK (scanned 30 workflow file(s), 53 job(s), 26 job-level if: expression(s); 10 read needs.*.outputs.*, all naming a status function).
✓ check-required-contexts: 6 required context name(s) pinned across 2 workflow(s); 5 instruction surface(s) scanned against 2 retired name(s).
✓ check:declared-population-live — 156 of 200 famil(ies) declare a path population, and every one of them reaches this tree's 7879 tracked file(s).
```

Reconciliation is machine-checked, not arithmetic by hand — `node scripts/pm/dispatch-gates.mjs --ran ran.list` over a record built from `--commands` output, so both sides are strings the tool itself emitted:

```
Run reconciliation — 21 derived, 21 run, 0 NOT-MEASURED, 0 UNRUN.
✓ dispatch-gates --ran: 21 derived famil(ies) accounted for — 21 run, 0 NOT-MEASURED.
```

Also run as the standing devx-tooling extras: `pnpm check:ratchet-remedy-authority` (PASS — "183 scripts swept"), `pnpm check:declared-population-live` (PASS, also inside the 21).

One note on how the `check:pm-dispatch-gates` row was reached, because it is the row this reconciliation is most often lied to about. Its first run in this container was killed at the ~10 minute foreground ceiling (`exit 143`, no verdict printed). That is **NOT MEASURED**, not a pass and not a fail — and `parseRunRecord`'s own header records a card where exactly that kill was written off as NOT-MEASURED and came back green on a complete run. So it was re-run to completion instead of being claimed: `os-verify-lock` slot `issue-9709`, waited 7m35s, held 12m57s, `command-exit 0`, `✓ dispatch-gates self-test: 1232 cases pass.` The `--ran` record above therefore carries no NOT-MEASURED claim at all.

## Changeset

**None — `skip-changeset`.** This diff is one workflow file; it publishes nothing from any package, which is `changeset-check`'s own stated criterion for the exemption ("this PR declares no release of its own"; `pr-automation.yml` job `changeset-check`). `lint.yml` names "this PR edits a CI-internal script" as the textbook case. The label is applied on this PR and read back.

## Not touched, deliberately

`ci.yml` (already correct, and it is the reference this copies), `scripts/check-console-injection.mjs`, `scripts/build-console.sh` (held by an in-flight card), and `release.yml`'s pnpm-store / turbo cache steps. The scope fence for this card is `.github/workflows/release.yml` alone.

`ci.yml` also carries an "Assert a real Console dist is in place" step before `check:console-sha`, which this PR does **not** copy. It is not needed here: `--require-stamp` already makes a missing dist and an unstamped dist fatal (`check-console-injection.mjs` exit-code contract, plus its self-test cases "no dist fails when required" and "unstamped is fatal when required"), which is what that step exists to prevent in `ci.yml`'s bare invocation.
